title: Evaluation case
description: One query put to Recall, plus the policy assertions it makes. A case carries no answers: relevance judgments live in a separate file so a runner can hand an agent the queries while withholding the answers.

case_id.description: Stable within a pack. Judgments key on it.

as_of.description: Historical boundary. Fixture runs inject the clock from this value.

tags.description: Reporting groups. Metrics are reported per tag so a large group cannot hide a small one.

expected_fail.description: Which of this case's assertions are known to fail today, and what has to land before they can hold. It names assertions rather than excusing the case, because a case-wide exemption also excuses regressions nobody predicted, and because a case waiting on two tickets must be able to show movement when either one lands. Every assertion the case declares and does not name here is enforced as on any other case. A run in which a named assertion stopped failing fails the expected_failures_current gate, so a marking cannot outlive its defect.

reason.description: What has to land, in enough words to be actionable. An expected-failure list with nothing to wait on is a mute button.

assertions.description: The excused assertion fields, spelled as the assertions block spells them. A name outside this vocabulary excuses nothing; a name the case does not declare can never be violated. Both are rejected by recall eval validate.

mode.description: Invocation mode. Defaults to explicit; a case testing suppression must say pre_reply, because suppression applies to a host's passive budget and never hides evidence somebody asked for.

suppress_lineages.description: Lineage roots the host has already shown. Suppression state belongs to the host, so a case that tests it supplies the state.

scope.description: Request scope, the way a caller would narrow it.

behavior.description: What the case expects Recall to do. The vocabulary matches recall.Outcome one for one: an earlier draft had a 'clarify' behavior with no outcome behind it, so a case expecting it could never pass. Deciding to ask a follow-up question is something a host does with what Recall returned.

source_uid.description: Immutable source identity. The locator separator is forbidden inside it.

assertions.description: Policy assertions. These are not relevance judgments: they state what the run must report, not which evidence is good.

expected_coverage.description: Ground truth for coverage accuracy: degraded must be reported when and only when this says degraded.

expected_revisions.description: A returned locator for one of these lineage roots must expand to the named source revision.

withheld_lineages.description: Lineage roots that must be reported as withheld, keyed to the suppression reason that must have withheld them. suppressed_lineages asks only about the host's own already-shown list; this asks about any rule that removes a result, so a rule whose whole job is to withhold something can be measured doing it rather than inferred from a smaller count.

expected_top_lineage.description: The lineage root that must rank first. Graded metrics score the shape of a whole list, so none of them can say which single record is the answer — which is the entire claim some queries make, and the one a caller reading only the first result sees.

min_results.description: Fewest results the response may carry. A caller pays for every result it is handed, so the count is part of the contract.

max_results.description: Most results the response may carry. Zero is a real bound: a case that must abstain says 0.

max_results_per_record.description: How many result slots one record may occupy. Identity is the source record id together with the content fingerprint, across sources: one record reached through two source instances is one thing a caller has to read, not two. A result missing either half is its own record, because identity claimed without evidence would collapse results that merely lack a fingerprint.

excerpt_contains.description: Substrings that must appear, case-insensitively, in the excerpt shown for a lineage root. The only assertion about what a result says rather than where it ranked: a hit whose displayed text does not contain the term that matched cannot be judged without a second call.
